name: CoreWeave
snippet: Nasdaq-listed GPU cloud that rents NVIDIA capacity to AI labs, hyperscalers and trading firms. It ended June 2026 with a $104B revenue backlog and 1.5 GW of active power.
origin: Michael Intrator, Brian Venturo, Brannin McBee and Peter Salanki founded the company in New Jersey in 2017 as Atlantic Crypto, an Ethereum miner that ran on GPUs. After crypto prices fell in 2018, they renamed it CoreWeave in 2019 and began renting the same GPUs as cloud compute. CoreWeave listed on Nasdaq in March 2025 and completed its purchase of Weights & Biases in May 2025. Its $9B all-stock bid for Core Scientific ended in October 2025 after Core Scientific shareholders voted it down.
today: CoreWeave reported Q2 2026 revenue of $2.58B, up 112% from a year earlier, and a net loss of $626M. Its revenue backlog stood at $104B on June 30, and management said customers added more than $25B of new commitments early in Q3. The company ran 1.5 GW of active power at the end of June and had 4.2 GW under contract by its August earnings call. Microsoft supplied 67% of 2025 revenue, and the three largest customers made up 72% of Q2 2026 revenue. Meta has committed about $35B across two contracts, OpenAI up to $22.4B, and Jane Street about $6B plus a $1B equity investment. CoreWeave guides to 2026 revenue of $12.4B to $13.2B and capex of $35B to $39B, and its total debt reached $35.6B in June.
platform: CoreWeave runs Kubernetes-native bare-metal clusters and offers SUNK, its Slurm on Kubernetes service for large training jobs, along with Mission Control for fleet health and Weights & Biases for experiment tracking. CoreWeave says it was the first cloud to complete bring-up and validation of an NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 rack, in June 2026, using Dell servers plus its own Valvey liquid-cooling valves and Racky rack controllers. In Q2 2026 it launched CoreWeave Interconnect to Google Cloud, SUNK Anywhere and cross-cloud LOTA data caching. Booked ARR for its managed inference service grew past $100M, and the company targets more than $250M by the end of 2026.
outlook: CoreWeave expects more than 1.85 GW of active power by the end of 2026 and targets more than 8 GW by 2030. It is expanding into Asia with 360 MW of contracted capacity in Indonesia due in 2028 and a 240 MW lease at an AdaniConneX campus in Navi Mumbai, India, with first power aimed at mid-2028. Interest expense rose to $640M in Q2 2026, and the company guides to $860M to $940M for Q3. NVIDIA bought $2B of CoreWeave stock in January 2026 and agreed to help it secure land and power for more than 5 GW of AI factories by 2030.

name: Nebius
aka: Nebius Group N.V., formerly Yandex N.V.
snippet: Amsterdam-based AI cloud built from the international businesses of Yandex. Its run-rate revenue hit $3.0B in June 2026, and Meta and Microsoft hold contracts worth up to $27B and $19.4B.
origin: Nebius is what remained of Yandex N.V., the Dutch parent of the Russian search company, after it sold its Russian businesses to a Russian consortium for about $5.4B in July 2024. The company kept the businesses that operated outside Russia, including its AI cloud unit, and renamed itself Nebius Group in August 2024. Its shares resumed trading on Nasdaq on October 21, 2024, after a suspension that began in February 2022. Yandex founder Arkady Volozh leads the company as CEO.
today: Nebius reported Q2 2026 revenue of $582.3M, up 454% year over year, and annualized run-rate revenue of $3.0B at the end of June. It guides to 2026 revenue of $3B to $3.4B, year-end ARR of $7B to $9B and capex of $20B to $25B. Microsoft signed a five-year contract in September 2025 worth $17.4B, or up to $19.4B with options, served from a new site in Vineland, New Jersey. Meta followed a $3B contract in 2025 with a five-year agreement in March 2026 worth up to $27B, with delivery starting in early 2027. Reflection AI signed a compute deal of more than $1B in July 2026, and Q2 also brought large contracts with Cohere, a new US lab and a US quantitative trading firm. NVIDIA agreed to invest $2B in March 2026 and disclosed a 9.3% stake in July. Management expects about $9B of customer prepayments in 2026, which cover a large share of its capex.
platform: Nebius runs its own cloud software stack, branded Aether, with GPU virtual machines, managed Kubernetes and Slurm through Soperator, its open-source Kubernetes operator for Slurm. Token Factory is its managed inference and fine-tuning service for open models, and in 2026 Nebius bought Eigen AI for about $643M and Inferize to strengthen inference, plus Tavily to add agentic search. In December 2025 it launched HGX B300 and GB300 NVL72 capacity in Finland and says it was the first cloud in Europe to run GB300 NVL72 in production. Palantir named Nebius its preferred sovereign AI infrastructure partner in September 2026 and plans to integrate Nebius compute and inference into its platform.
outlook: Nebius raised its year-end 2026 contracted power target from more than 3 GW in February to 5 GW in August, and it aims for 800 MW to 1 GW of connected power by the end of 2026. It plans to bring more than 1 GW online each year from 2027 and expects Vera Rubin systems in late 2026 or early 2027. New sites include a 240 MW former Bridgestone tyre plant in Béthune, France, a project in Birmingham, Alabama, a 50 MW, 12-year lease from AIB Data Centers in the southeastern US, and a letter of intent for a large share of a planned 600 MW campus on Rotterdam's Maasvlakte. It also runs or leases capacity in Finland, the UK, Israel, Iceland, Paris and Kansas City.

name: Lambda
snippet: GPU cloud that began by selling deep learning workstations. Reuters reported a $35B Anthropic contract in September 2026, and Lambda is reportedly raising up to $4B before a planned 2027 IPO.
origin: Stephen and Michael Balaban founded Lambda in 2012. The company first sold GPU workstations and servers to machine learning researchers, then launched Lambda Cloud to rent NVIDIA GPUs by the hour, and cloud rental now provides most of its revenue. It has worked with Microsoft for more than eight years and now markets itself as the Superintelligence Cloud.
today: Reuters reported in September 2026 that Anthropic signed a $35B cloud agreement with Lambda for about 350 MW at a campus that Hut 8 is building in Nueces County, Texas, where NVIDIA holds the lease. The Wall Street Journal reported in October that the deal lifted Lambda's backlog from about $15B in June to about $50B in September. The same report said Lambda is raising up to $4B at a $14.5B pre-money valuation, led by Blackstone and Coatue, as its last private round before a planned 2027 IPO. Microsoft signed a multibillion-dollar agreement in November 2025 for tens of thousands of NVIDIA GPUs, including GB300 NVL72 systems. Lambda raised $2.93B of debt in 2026 through a $1B credit facility in May, a $926M term loan B in August and a $1.008B investment-grade term loan in October. The October loan carries a 6.78% fixed rate and funds three deployments for two investment-grade customers. Michel Combes is CEO, and co-founder Stephen Balaban is CTO.
platform: Lambda sells on-demand GPU instances, 1-Click Clusters of HGX B200 and H100 nodes with fully managed Kubernetes or Slurm and S3-compatible storage, and single-tenant GB300 NVL72 superclusters on Quantum-2 InfiniBand. Its site lists Vera Rubin NVL72, GB300 NVL72, HGX B300, HGX B200, H200 and H100 systems. Lambda also builds its own AI factories, including a 24 MW Kansas City site planned around more than 10,000 Blackwell Ultra GPUs for one customer and a new campus in Mayes County, Oklahoma.
outlook: Lambda plans its IPO for 2027, subject to execution and market conditions. If the reported figures hold, Anthropic accounts for about $35B of a roughly $50B backlog. The Kansas City site can scale past 100 MW, and Lambda has pledged to pay 100% of the energy costs of its Oklahoma campus, which will use closed-loop cooling.

name: Crusoe
snippet: AI infrastructure company that builds energy-first campuses and runs Crusoe Cloud. It raised $3.9B at a $30.9B valuation in September 2026 and reports over $140B of contracted value.
origin: Chase Lochmiller and Cully Cavness founded Crusoe in Denver in 2018 to mine Bitcoin with natural gas that oil wells would otherwise flare. The company applied the same approach of placing compute next to cheap, stranded power to GPUs, launched Crusoe Cloud, and then moved into building large AI campuses. It sold its Bitcoin mining business to NYDIG in 2025 to focus on AI infrastructure.
today: Crusoe developed the 1.2 GW, eight-building Stargate campus in Abilene, Texas, used by OpenAI, under a $15B joint venture with Blue Owl Capital and Primary Digital Infrastructure. In March 2026 it announced a separate 900 MW Abilene campus for Microsoft, with the first building due to be energized in mid-2027, which would bring the full Abilene site to about 2.1 GW. It is also building a campus for Google in Armstrong County, Texas, and in July 2026 announced a 1 GW campus with Lancium in Childress, Texas. The Series F initial close in September 2026 raised $3.9B at a $30.9B post-money valuation, co-led by Atreides Management, Mubadala Capital and Valor Equity Partners, after a $1.38B Series E at $10B in October 2025. Crusoe reports over $140B of total contracted value, more than 6 GW of gross contracted capacity and 1 GW delivered and operational. TechCrunch reported a $13B, five-year cloud contract with Jane Street and said Crusoe has met with Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley about a possible IPO.
platform: Crusoe Cloud offers GPU instances, AutoClusters, managed Kubernetes and managed Slurm on NVIDIA GB200 NVL72, HGX B200, H200 and H100 systems and on AMD MI355X and MI300X. Crusoe Managed Inference has more than $100M of contracted ARR, and in July 2026 the company added serverless fine-tuning and self-serve inference deployments. Crusoe Spark units are modular data centers that travel by truck and connect to large power sources. The company makes its own switchgear and other electrical equipment in two Tulsa, Oklahoma factories that total about 1 million square feet.
outlook: Crusoe says it will use the Series F to scale existing programs and to build its own AI factories, from large campuses to Spark units. The Microsoft campus relies on a dedicated 900 MW on-site power plant with battery storage, and its first building is not due until mid-2027. Crusoe has also signed ON.energy to supply 5 GW of AI UPS systems and Aalo Atomics to pursue a nuclear-powered AI factory.

name: Fluidstack
snippet: AI infrastructure company that builds and runs dedicated compute for frontier labs. It is the build partner for Anthropic's $50B US data center program, with sites in Texas and New York.
origin: Fluidstack started in 2017 with roots in Oxford and grew as a UK-based GPU cloud for AI companies. It became one of the first third-party providers to host Google's custom TPUs and worked with Meta, Mistral and Black Forest Labs. After Anthropic chose it to build custom data centers in November 2025, Fluidstack moved its global headquarters to New York City in December 2025.
today: Anthropic selected Fluidstack in November 2025 to deliver custom data centers in Texas and New York under a $50B US build program, with sites coming online through 2026. Fluidstack closed an $830M Series A at a $7.5B valuation in January 2026, led by Situational Awareness, and Bloomberg reported in April 2026 that it was in talks to raise $1B at an $18B valuation. At TeraWulf's Lake Mariner campus in New York it leases about 360 MW, and Google backstops about $3.2B of the related project debt. In Texas it is building a $4B first phase in Cameron County, and in July 2026 it led the purchase of TeraWulf's 50.1% stake in their 168 MW Abernathy joint venture. Fluidstack withdrew from a €10B French AI project in March 2026.
platform: Fluidstack builds and operates dedicated clusters and data centers for AI labs, governments and enterprises. It says it can take a 250 MW facility from groundbreaking to operation in six months and designs its sites around closed-loop cooling.
outlook: Fluidstack says it aims to deploy hundreds of gigawatts of compute for AI labs over the next five years. Anthropic is its most significant customer relationship, and Google credit support underpins its leases at TeraWulf sites. The company plans more US hiring in Austin and San Francisco in 2026.

name: Nscale
snippet: London-based AI cloud spun out of Arkon Energy in 2024. It filed for a NYSE IPO in September 2026 and reports over $103B of contracted value, led by Microsoft and Anthropic.
origin: Nscale was spun out of Arkon Energy in May 2024, with Josh Payne as founder and CEO. It began with a 60 MW AI data center plan in Glomfjord, Norway, and pitched itself as a vertically integrated AI hyperscaler running on renewable power. In July 2025 it formed Stargate Norway with Aker and OpenAI, a 50/50 Aker and Nscale venture in Narvik, and in September 2025 it raised a $1.1B Series B.
today: Nscale filed for a New York Stock Exchange IPO under the symbol NSCL on September 18, 2026. Its S-1 reports revenue of $33.0M in 2025 and $140.6M in the first half of 2026, with a first-half net loss of $1.02B. As of August 31, 2026 it had about 25,000 active GPUs, 461,000 active and contracted GPUs, about 1.37 GW of active and contracted capacity and $103.4B of active and contracted TCV. Anthropic signed GPU services agreements worth up to about $44.6B in August 2026 for the Monarch campus in Mason County, West Virginia. Microsoft contracted about 200,000 NVIDIA GB300 GPUs in October 2025 across Texas, Portugal, the UK and Norway, and in 2026 added more than 66,000 Vera Rubin GPUs in Sines, Portugal, and a letter of intent for 1.35 GW at Monarch. Nscale raised a $2B Series C at a $14.6B valuation in March 2026 and $3.36B in pre-IPO convertible notes in September 2026, including a $1B NVIDIA commitment due in November. The company says it deployed 24,000 GPUs in September 2026 alone and runs six active data centers in five countries.
platform: Nscale's cloud offers bare metal, the Nscale Kubernetes Service, managed Slurm, serverless inference and fine-tuning. In July 2026 it agreed to buy Anyscale, the company behind the open-source Ray framework, which will keep its brand and existing customers. It bought Future-tech in December 2025 to speed data center delivery and American Intelligence & Power Corporation, the company behind the Monarch campus, in March 2026.
outlook: Monarch is planned around 2 GW of on-site Caterpillar gas generation by the first half of 2028, with Vera Rubin deployments starting in late 2027. Nscale says it controls more than 10 GW of power pipeline and plans to bring more than 100,000 Vera Rubin GPUs to Europe in 2027. Its first-half 2026 net loss of $1.02B is about seven times its revenue for the period, and its S-1 warns that a small number of customers drive much of its revenue.

name: Together AI
snippet: Inference and GPU cloud built on open-source AI research. It raised an $800M Series C in July 2026 and says investors have capitalized more than 500 MW of compute for it.
origin: Vipul Ved Prakash, Ce Zhang, Chris Ré, Percy Liang and Tri Dao founded Together AI in 2022 around open-source AI research. Prakash is CEO, Zhang is CTO and Dao, who created FlashAttention, is chief scientist. The company built its business on serving and tuning open-source models and then added GPU clusters for customers that train their own models.
today: Together AI raised an $800M Series C in July 2026 with investors including Aramco Ventures, NVIDIA, Vista Equity, General Catalyst and Salesforce Ventures, and says investors have capitalized more than 500 MW of independent compute for it. That round followed a $305M Series B at a $3.3B valuation in February 2025, when it announced a 36,000-GPU GB200 NVL72 cluster with Hypertec and 200 MW of secured power. In October 2026 it said it serves hundreds of trillions of tokens a month to more than one million developers. The same month it became the first customer of a dedicated B300 inference cluster on IBM Cloud.
platform: Together AI sells serverless and dedicated inference for open models, fine-tuning and post-training APIs, and Together GPU Clusters. Clusters offer H100, H200, HGX B200 and HGX B300 nodes on demand up to 256 GPUs, and reserved GB200 and GB300 NVL72 systems scale past 4,000 GPUs. Customers choose managed Kubernetes or Slurm on Kubernetes, with InfiniBand networking and WEKA or VAST file storage. Its research team ships kernels such as FlashAttention-4 for Blackwell and the Together Megakernel.
outlook: Together AI says it will use the Series C to speed adoption of open-source models and to support expected compute growth. It serves Moonshot AI's Kimi models through a partnership and launched Together Link in October 2026 to run open models inside the coding tools developers already use. The company has not disclosed revenue or the Series C valuation.

name: TensorWave
snippet: AMD-only GPU cloud based in Las Vegas. In August 2026 it signed a $6.5B, 15-year lease for 222 MW at Fermi America's Project Matador campus in Texas.
origin: TensorWave launched in 2023 as a cloud that rents only AMD Instinct GPUs, starting with the MI300X, to give AI teams an alternative to NVIDIA-based clouds. It raised a $43M round in October 2024 and that month signed a 1 GW infrastructure agreement with Tecfusions. CEO Darrick Horton co-founded the company, and AMD is among its investors.
today: TensorWave signed a $6.5B, 15-year lease in August 2026 as the first binding customer of Fermi America's Project Matador campus in Carson County, Texas, starting with a 222 MW facility for tens of thousands of AMD Instinct GPUs. Expansion rights for two more buildings could take its total there past 650 MW. The Wall Street Journal reported in June 2026 that a new funding round valued TensorWave at $1.55B, and the company says it has raised more than $500M in total. Its investors include AMD, Magnetar, Maverick Silicon, Nexus Venture Partners and Atreides Management. It opened a new Las Vegas headquarters in April 2026 and expanded its executive team in September 2026.
platform: TensorWave offers bare-metal AMD MI300X, MI325X and MI355X systems with managed Kubernetes, managed Slurm, network storage and fleet observability. Its site lists the MI455X as new, and in July 2026 it announced AMD Helios rack-scale systems for cloud customers. The company holds ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type 2 and HIPAA certifications.
outlook: TensorWave's growth depends on AMD's GPU roadmap and on Fermi America finishing the Matador campus on schedule. The Helios and MI455X rollout is the next product step to watch.

name: Voltage Park
snippet: H100 cloud launched in 2023 that merged with Lightning AI in January 2026. The combined company runs more than 36,000 owned H100, B200 and GB300 GPUs under the Lightning AI name.

facts.label: Data centers
facts.value: Six Tier 3+ sites in four US states

origin: Voltage Park started in 2023 with backing from the Navigation Fund, a philanthropy funded by Jed McCaleb, to rent H100 capacity to AI startups and researchers at lower prices. It launched with about 24,000 NVIDIA H100 SXM5 GPUs on 3.2 Tbps InfiniBand, and early customers included Imbue, Character.ai and Atomic AI.
today: Lightning AI completed a merger with Voltage Park in January 2026, and the combined company operates under the Lightning AI name with William Falcon as CEO and former Voltage Park CEO Ozan Kaya as president. The merged company says it owns and operates more than 36,000 H100, B200 and GB300 GPUs and grew from $18M to more than $500M of ARR since 2024. Its GPUs sit in six Tier 3+ data centers across four US states.
platform: Voltage Park sells on-demand and reserved NVIDIA GPUs with bare-metal access, virtual machines, managed Kubernetes, storage and observability, with on-demand prices starting at $1.99 per hour. Lightning AI adds its developer platform from the makers of PyTorch Lightning, so customers can train, fine-tune, deploy and serve models on the same infrastructure.
outlook: The combined company plans to sell one platform that covers GPU access, training, deployment and inference. It has not disclosed a valuation or deal terms for the merger.

name: Cirrascale Cloud Services
snippet: San Diego cloud for private AI that runs NVIDIA, AMD, Qualcomm and Tenstorrent hardware. In 2026 it released its multi-vendor Inference Platform and began offering Gemini on Google Distributed Cloud.
origin: Cirrascale Cloud Services is a San Diego company that rents dedicated multi-GPU servers and high-speed storage for AI training and inference, backed by professional and managed services. It hosts accelerators from several vendors, including NVIDIA, AMD, Qualcomm and Tenstorrent, and describes itself as a neocloud built for private AI.
today: Cirrascale released the production version of its Cirrascale Inference Platform in September 2026, which routes requests across NVIDIA, AMD, Qualcomm and Tenstorrent hardware and supports open, private and Gemini models. In April 2026 it began offering Gemini on Google Distributed Cloud, and in March it became an implementation partner for Google Public Sector's research program and launched Cirrascale Government Services. It added Tenstorrent Galaxy Blackhole systems in May 2026 and partnered with Telehouse in July to place inference closer to enterprise data.
platform: The company sells dedicated multi-GPU servers, high-speed storage and managed services, with no ingress or egress fees. Its AI Innovation Cloud added NVIDIA HGX B200 and AMD Instinct MI350 series systems in 2025, and it plans to offer AMD Helios racks with MI455X and MI430X GPUs once AMD makes them generally available. The Inference Platform includes governance aligned with HIPAA, SOC 2 and FedRAMP and supports fine-tuning on private data.
outlook: Cirrascale targets enterprise and public-sector inference that must run in private environments, and its government division works toward HIPAA, FERPA, CMMC 2.0 and FedRAMP High requirements. Its Helios offering depends on when AMD reaches general availability.

name: Denvr Dataworks
snippet: Calgary GPU cloud that builds its own liquid- and immersion-cooled clusters and sells sovereign compute in Canada. It reported more than US$10M of ARR in April 2026 and has reserved about 1 GW in Alberta.

facts.label: Reserved power
facts.value: About 1 GW at two Alberta sites

origin: Geoff Gordon and Kyle McCrindle founded Denvr Dataworks in Calgary in mid-2017 and have funded it mostly from earlier profits. The company builds and assembles its own hardware rather than renting colocation space, and it has run a commercial AI cloud since 2022.
today: The Logic reported in April 2026 that Denvr had raised US$12.5M of equity, deployed about US$100M of infrastructure on its own account and passed US$10M of ARR. It runs a facility in southeast Calgary and has reserved about 1 GW of capacity across two Alberta sites that it has not fully built. The company competes for Canadian federal and Alberta government work in defence, health and sovereignty, and planned to add infrastructure later in 2026.
platform: Denvr sells on-demand and reserved GPUs as bare metal, virtual machines or containers, managed inference endpoints with an OpenAI-compatible API, and NVMe shared storage. Its clusters scale to 1,024 GPUs on 3,200 Gbps InfiniBand. With UNICOM Engineering it has run an immersion-cooled NVIDIA H200 platform in production since April 2024 at 14 servers per rack. Its Canada AI Platform bundles hardware, models and cloud services for sovereign deployments.
outlook: Denvr plans to grow in modular blocks of 1 MW to 5 MW and to bid for Canadian sovereign and defence AI work with partners in its CAIP Defence Coalition.
